chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Ali from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed li'an (oath of elimination) with his wife while she was pregnant, and her pregnancy had become evident, and he denied what was in her womb. When she gave birth, he claimed the child and acknowledged it, and asserted that it was from him. He said: The child is returned to him, and he inherits from her, and he is not lashed, because the li'an has concluded.
ai.seo_question: What are the legal rulings on li'an when the wife is pregnant and the husband later acknowledges the child?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies that the li'an process is considered complete and binding once initiated during pregnancy, even if the husband later acknowledges paternity after the child's birth. Consequently, the husband is exempt from the hadd punishment of lashing, as the procedural requirement has been fulfilled, and the child is legally attributed to him for inheritance purposes. This highlights the Shia juristic view that li'an establishes lineage and excludes inheritance rights for the husband, with the timing of acknowledgment affecting the penalty but not the attribution.
